source.title: Vaccine: Perturbation-aware Alignment for Large Language Models against Harmful Fine-tuning Attack
source.authors: Tian-Sheng Huang; Si-Hao Hu; Ling Liu

record.tranche_reason: Tests the effect of supervised fine-tuning an aligned model on mixed benign and harmful user data and measures harmful outputs, using a direct harmful-fine-tuning intervention in additional models and settings.
record.gate_note: Reports harmful scores after fine-tuning on harmful/benign mixtures and after clean user fine-tuning; these measure the behavior named by V1 and V2. It also reports hidden-embedding drift as a proposed mechanism. No tests of response-position KL, compliant-prefill or other opening bypasses, safety parameters/ranks, or token-depth training are reported. Other defense-method comparisons are not cataloged here; their findings are not needed to identify the SFT harmful-fine-tuning results or Vaccine’s own results recorded below.
record.test_reason: Its SFT-aligned baseline results measure harmful score after user fine-tuning with 0–20% BeaverTails harmful data mixed into task data. That bears on V1 and V2, using a different recipe from Qi et al.: LoRA, a self-aligned base Llama2-7B and a moderation-model judge. Appendix B.3 explicitly disputes Qi et al.'s benign-fine-tuning finding. Most other tables compare the authors' own Vaccine defence.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors go further than 'proposed': they call harmful embedding drift 'the cause' of broken alignment, while elsewhere calling it a conjecture. They say a few harmful examples 'can easily' break alignment, though their own SFT numbers show modest rises. They restate Qi et al.'s benign finding as 'may not necessarily degrade' safety, depending on model and dataset. Vaccine cuts HS by up to 9.8 points vs SFT, with the gain shrinking at high ratios and larger sample counts.
record.recipe_differences: Uses aligned-model SFT followed by user SFT on mixed benign task data and BeaverTails harmful examples, then measures harmful score. It evaluates its own perturbation-aware alignment defense and uses its stated default datasets, prompt construction, and LoRA implementations; it does not establish an exact reproduction of the original study’s complete recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with harmful-data ratio, user-data sample count, model, downstream dataset, and Single- versus Double-LoRA implementation. The study also reports that Vaccine’s benefit diminishes at high harmful ratios and larger sample counts.

fits_no_version.finding: L2 drift of hidden embeddings on alignment data after user fine-tuning grows with harmful ratio. It is larger for the SFT-aligned than the non-aligned model and coincides in training step with the rise in alignment loss (figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful fine-tuning degrades alignment by shifting hidden representations of alignment inputs.

record.problems: The study reports harmful score rather than refusal rate and generally does not provide uncertainty estimates or error bars. For clean benign fine-tuning, a pre-user-fine-tuning HS baseline is not stated alongside the reported table value. Results use a limited set of models and user-task datasets; authors note the task and SFT-only alignment limitations.
record.rows_left_out: At most 60 rows retained. Not cataloged: baseline comparison methods other than Vaccine (Non-Aligned, EWC, Vlguard, and KL), fine-tune-accuracy outcomes, alignment-loss measurements, system-resource measurements, and Vaccine hyperparameter/random-perturbation tables. These are defense-method, utility, mechanism, or resource comparisons rather than additional direct SFT-versus-harmful-data outcomes for V1/V2. No numerical embedding-drift values are available in the text; the plot-only findings are represented in r48–r49.

untested.parts: Harmful-only fine-tuning; full-parameter fine-tuning; RLHF- or chat-aligned models (e.g. Llama-2-chat, GPT-3.5); refusal-rate or GPT-4-judge outcomes; higher learning rates (authors note larger LR strengthens the harmful effect).
Carefully selected benign data; instruction-style benign data such as Alpaca/Dolly on a safety-trained chat model. SST2's one-word labels are, by the authors' own account, not instruction-like.
Per-token KL across response positions: not tested.
Prefilling, suffixes or decoding attacks: not tested.
Localization of safety in weights or ranks: not tested.
Causes of shallowness: not tested. Embedding drift is offered as a cause of fine-tuning degradation, not of shallowness.
Token-depth safety training: not tested. Vaccine perturbs embeddings, not response depth.

missing.what: Vaccine-aligned model HS before any user fine-tuning (43.80), versus 48.20 SST2, 47.80 AGNEWS and 69.40 GSM8K after default harmful-mixed fine-tuning. This is the only pre-fine-tuning safety reference in the paper and shows a 25.6-point rise on GSM8K.
Clean-data fine-tuning statement for all three datasets and different sample numbers, with no numbers given.
Figure 2a: SFT vs non-aligned HS across harmful ratios, and the claim that a small harmful ratio significantly downgrades alignment (figure only).
Learning-rate sensitivity: authors report a larger LR makes the harmful effect stronger, but no numbers are given.

record.verdict_notes: The record labelled V1 'supports' and also gave V2 a duplicate limits_scope on the same row; both are revised. Key caveats: (1) the SFT-aligned model's HS before fine-tuning is never reported. The only comparison is clean-fine-tuned HS of 48.6, which already indicates weak LoRA alignment. (2) Table 3's model columns appear scrambled, and 'default' values disagree across Tables 1–4. (3) The B.3 dispute of Qi et al. is argued mainly from the non-aligned model's one-word outputs, which does not bear on safety-trained models. (4) About half the rows are Vaccine-vs-SFT comparisons and are relinked to none. T5 would also be defensible given the explicit restatement of the benign claim.

versions.untested_parts: Tests harmful examples mixed with benign user data, including 10–200 harmful examples at n=1000 and other sample-count settings. It does not test harmful-only fine-tuning or directly report refusal rates; its outcome is moderation-model harmful score.
Tests clean benign task data, principally SST2, and discusses results across simulated datasets. It does not test carefully selected benign data as a distinct intervention.
The study proposes harmful embedding drift as a cause of safety degradation, but does not test why safety would be shallow or whether data/objectives produce first-token concentration.
Vaccine trains perturbation-aware alignment but does not test whether safety is spread beyond the first tokens or whether token-depth training holds up.

relationships.condition: LoRA SFT-aligned Llama2-7B, SST2 user data, lr 1e-5, BeaverTails moderation HS
relationships.reason: HS rises with harmful examples but stays far from full compliance. Clean fine-tuning gives 48.6; 10/50/100/200 harmful examples give +1.2/+4.0/+6.6/+11.4 (r2–r5), and 25–125 examples at p=0.05 reach 61.4 (r10–r14). The comparison point is a clean-fine-tuned model already ~49% harmful.
relationships.display_finding: Clean fine-tuning already gave a harmful score of 48.6. Adding 10, 50, 100 or 200 harmful examples raised it by only 1.2, 4.0, 6.6 or 11.4 points, and 25–125 examples at p=0.05 reached 61.4.
